review_basis:
A fresh, previously-untouched real project this session: a VA (Bldg 47, Asheville NC) EHRM Infrastructure renovation set, sheet 47-PP401 (page 66) carrying many individually-scattered `3/4"`/`1"`/`1 1/4" CD` (condensate drain) callouts and a couple of `1/2" CW` domestic-water callouts, unlike the tightly-paired parallel supply/return racks this session has already learned to distrust on other sheets. A grid sweep of eleven of these labels found six real, size-bound `trace_run` hits; five of the six carried a non-standard `custom`-class elbow angle (52.8, 65.3, 62.8, 61.2, 33.9 degrees) -- this session's own established red flag for a leader-line mistrace, matching the same pathology already confirmed twice more this same day on two different fresh projects -- and were set aside without individual crop verification, this sheet's own drafting convention evidently favoring diagonal `CD` leader stubs near its labels.

The one candidate WITHOUT that red flag (13.57 LF, `pipe:0.75`, `CD`, `dead_end`/`ambiguous`, one genuine 90-degree elbow) was confirmed via marked render crop: a real, straight, solid black vertical pipe drop running from a real ceiling-penetration point (the forward `dead_end`, at a red-hatched fire-rated wall/ceiling boundary) straight down through two office rooms' own wall lines, through one real 90-degree elbow, to the point where it joins the sheet's own main horizontal condensate header (the backward `ambiguous` stop, a real branch-into-header tie-in feeding an IDU indoor fan-coil unit below, not an arbitrary cut). The sheet's own printed `3/4" CD` label sits directly beside this exact run via its own short diagonal leader, which was checked separately and confirmed to terminate on the SAME horizontal header near the tie-in point, not on some other, different line -- unlike this same day's two rejected leader-line candidates on other projects, this label's own leader and the traced pipe agree on which line is real.
scope: A single real 3/4" CD (condensate drain) branch line (13.57 LF, one 90-degree elbow) on VA Project 637's own sheet 47-PP401 (page 66), from a real ceiling-penetration dead end down to the real point where it ties into the sheet's own main condensate header serving an IDU fan-coil unit. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: five other `CD`/`CW` candidates found on this same sheet, all carrying a non-standard elbow angle and set aside as likely leader-line mistraces without individual verification (a real, disclosed opportunity for a more careful future pass, not confirmed rejections); every other `CD`/`CW` label on this same dense sheet not swept at all; every other sheet in this real 559-sheet project.
